info.description: Deploy and operate Remnawave fleets. Unofficial community project.

get.description: Answers while the process serves requests. It does not check dependencies.

503.description: At least one dependency is down.

get.description: Checks every configured dependency. Answers 503 with the same body shape when one is down.

The version of the running build and what the build recorded about itself: when and by which CI run it was made and the branch and revision it came from (`SW_BUILD_TIME`, `SW_BUILD_NUMBER`, `SW_GIT_BRANCH`, `SW_GIT_COMMIT`, set as build arguments of the image). What the build did not record is null. `git.commitUrl` is the page of the revision on GitHub, known when the revision is a hash.

get.summary: The newest release and the project page
get.description: For the version button and the project link of the console. The server asks GitHub for the latest release and the star count at most once a day and answers from its memory; the browser never calls GitHub. The request sends nothing that identifies the installation, the user or the browser. After a failed attempt the old answer is kept and the next attempt comes in an hour. The first call after the start does not wait more than a moment, so it may answer with nulls. `SW_UPDATE_CHECK=off` switches the check off: `enabled` is false and nothing is ever sent. Nothing is recorded in the audit log.
The OpenAPI 3.1 document generated from the route registry.
Lets the console choose between the first-run setup and the sign-in page.

post.summary: Create the instance owner
post.description: Works once, with the setup token the server printed to its log at start. Starts a session that still needs the authenticator to be set up (`/auth/totp/enrollment`).

post.summary: Sign in with a password
post.description: The first of two steps. On success a session cookie is set that is not yet usable for anything except finishing the sign-in. Wrong credentials and unknown users answer the same 401; repeated failures lock the account for a while (429).

post.summary: Finish signing in with an authenticator code or a recovery code
post.description: A recovery code works once. The session cookie is replaced by a new one when the sign-in completes.

post.summary: Get the authenticator secret

200.description: The secret to add to an authenticator.

post.description: Only before the authenticator was confirmed. Repeated calls return the same secret until it is confirmed.

post.summary: Confirm the authenticator and finish signing in
post.description: Returns the recovery codes. They are shown once and only their hashes are kept.

post.summary: Sign out
post.description: Ends the current session if there is one. Always answers 204.

post.summary: Prove the second factor again to elevate the session
post.description: Takes a code from the authenticator or a recovery code. For a short time afterwards the session may call the routes marked `x-sw-step-up`; they answer 403 `step_up_required` before that. A wrong code counts towards the lockout like a wrong code at sign-in. Signing in elevates the session already.

post.summary: Choose a password with an invitation token
post.description: For a new user or one whose credentials were reset. The token is used up. Starts a session that still needs the authenticator to be set up (`/auth/totp/enrollment`). An unknown, used or expired token answers 401.

post.summary: Change your own password
post.description: Needs the current password and an elevated session. Ends your other sessions and keeps this one. A wrong current password counts towards the lockout.

post.summary: Invite a user
post.description: Creates the account without a password and returns an invitation. The token is shown once. A taken login name or e-mail address answers 409.

patch.description: Role, status, display name and e-mail address. Refused with 409 when it would leave the instance without an active owner, or when you change your own role or status. Disabling a user ends their sessions.

delete.description: Removes the account with its password, authenticator, recovery codes, sessions, tokens and open invitation. Cannot be undone. Only a disabled account can be deleted (409 otherwise), and never your own (409). What the account did stays in the audit log under the name it had.

patch.description: The language the console uses for you after you sign in, on any browser. `null` goes back to following the browser.

post.summary: Reset the password and the authenticator of a user

200.description: The user and a new invitation.

post.description: Deletes the password, the authenticator and the recovery codes, ends every session of the user at once, and returns a new invitation. The user cannot sign in until it is accepted. Refused with 409 when you reset your own account (change your password instead).

get.summary: Whether the vault exists and is open
get.description: Also the number of secrets. Works while the vault is sealed.

post.summary: Set the vault up

201.description: The vault and its recovery key.

post.description: Once. Makes the key, wraps it under the passphrase and under a recovery key, and leaves the vault open. The recovery key is in the answer and nowhere else: it is the only way back in when the passphrase is lost. Answers 409 when a vault exists.

post.summary: Open the vault with the passphrase or the recovery key
post.description: A wrong passphrase or key answers 401 and is recorded; ten failures in fifteen minutes answer 429 for everyone.

post.summary: Close the vault
post.description: Wipes the key from memory. Nothing that needs a secret works until it is opened again.

get.summary: List the secrets, without their values
get.description: Works while the vault is sealed: names, types and dates are not secret.

post.summary: Store a secret
post.description: The vault must be open (423 `vault_sealed` otherwise). The value is encrypted with a key of its own and is write-only from now on. A taken name answers 409.

patch.summary: Rename a secret, change its details or replace its value
patch.description: A new `value` needs the vault open and moves the version forward; the old value is not kept. Renaming and the details work while sealed.

delete.description: Works while the vault is sealed. Cannot be undone. A secret that a server uses for its login or for sudo cannot be deleted: 409, naming the servers.

post.summary: Show the value of a secret
post.description: The only way a value leaves the vault. Needs the vault open, the reveal permission and a fresh second factor, and is recorded before the value is sent.

post.summary: Change the passphrase of the vault
post.description: Needs the current passphrase. The key that encrypts the secrets does not change, only the way the passphrase wraps it: nothing is re-encrypted, the recovery key stays valid, and the new passphrase is hardened with the current cost settings. Works while the vault is sealed. A wrong current passphrase answers 401 and counts towards the unseal limit.

post.summary: Issue a new recovery key
post.description: Needs the passphrase. The old recovery key stops working at once; the new one is in the answer and nowhere else, so keep it away from this server. Nothing is re-encrypted.

post.summary: Replace the key that wraps every data key

200.description: The new recovery key and the vault.

post.description: Needs the vault open and the passphrase. A new key-encryption key wraps every data key (the values are not re-encrypted), the key version moves forward, and a new recovery key is issued because the old one opened the old key. All or nothing: a failure leaves the vault as it was.

post.summary: Encrypt every secret under a fresh data key
post.description: Needs the vault open. Every current value is decrypted in memory and encrypted again under a new data key wrapped by the current key. Versions and values do not change. All or nothing.

get.summary: The roles and the permission catalogue
get.description: The built-in roles with the permissions each holds, and every permission with its meaning.
Newest first. Page back with `cursor`, or by page number with `offset`; `total` counts what the filters match. Filters combine.

schema.description: Return events older than this sequence number (`nextCursor` of the previous page).
Events to skip, newest first: the page number times `limit`, for a table with page numbers. With `cursor`, counted from there.

post.summary: Verify the integrity of the audit chain
post.description: Reads the whole log and checks the numbering, every link and every hash. The run is itself recorded. A broken chain is a normal answer (`ok: false`), not an error.

get.summary: Export the audit log for checking outside the database
get.description: Pages of events, oldest first, with every field their hashes cover, so that a copy can be verified without this server (`node dist/admin.js audit-verify <file>`). Each page is recorded. Needs a fresh second factor: a copy of the whole log is a lot to hand over.

schema.description: The first sequence number to return, 1 by default. Continue with `nextFrom` of the last page.

post.summary: Note the head of the audit chain in a form that cannot be made up in the database
post.description: Returns the last event with a signature made with a key that is not in the database. Keep the text somewhere else (a ticket, a vault of your own, a cron job). Later, a check against it proves that nothing up to that event was changed, and that no tail was cut off.

post.summary: Check the log against a checkpoint
post.description: Checks the signature, finds the event, compares its hash and checks the chain up to it. A failed check is a normal answer (`ok: false` with the reason). The check is recorded.

get.summary: The signed-in sessions of your account
get.description: Every active session of the caller, the current one marked.

delete.description: Ends another session of your own account at once. The session you are using cannot be ended here (409): sign out instead. A session that is not yours is reported as not found.

post.summary: End all your other sessions
post.description: Keeps the session you are using and ends every other session of your account.

get.summary: The signed-in sessions of every user
get.description: Active sessions, most recently used first. Filter by user with `userId`.

schema.description: Only the sessions of this user.

delete.summary: End a session of any user
delete.description: Ends the session at once and records it. The session you are using cannot be ended here (409).

post.summary: End every session of a user
post.description: Ends all sessions of the user at once, for example after a suspected theft of a cookie. Refused with 409 for your own account (use "end all other sessions").

get.description: The tokens issued in your name, active, expired and revoked ones, never their values.

delete.description: Stops the token at once. Revoking a token that is already revoked succeeds. A token of someone else is reported as not found.

post.summary: Create an API token in your own name
post.description: The token carries a subset of your permissions (never one that needs a fresh second factor), expires after at most a year, and may be limited to addresses. The value is in the answer and nowhere else: it is not stored and cannot be shown again.

get.summary: The API tokens of every user
get.description: Newest first. Filter by user with `userId`. Never the values.

schema.description: Only the tokens of this user.

delete.summary: Revoke the token of any user
delete.description: Stops the token at once and records it.

get.description: Reads the plugin directories on every call and says, for each plugin, what its files declare, what it asks for, and whether an administrator approved exactly that. A plugin that was enabled and whose files changed, went missing or became invalid is switched off here and the change is recorded.

post.summary: Enable a plugin and approve what it asks for
post.description: Approves the plugin as it is now: the digest of its files and the permissions of its manifest. The digest in the request is what the administrator was shown; if the files differ now the answer is 409 and nothing is enabled. Only a plugin that is usable can be enabled (not invalid, not for other versions of Swellwright).

post.summary: Disable a plugin
post.description: Switches the plugin off at once. The approval stays on record; enabling again needs a new approval of what the files are then. Disabling a plugin that is not enabled succeeds and changes nothing.

post.summary: Load an enabled plugin in its restricted process
post.description: Starts the plugin in a process of its own (no network, no child processes, only its own directory readable, a heap limit) and loads its modules; the answer says what loaded and which methods each module offers, or why it did not. The files are verified against the approval first: a plugin that is not what was approved is switched off instead. The process stays up until it is idle for a while, switched off, or changed.

get.description: The form the plugin declares (its `config.schema`) and what is set now. A secret field holds the id of a vault secret, never the secret.

put.summary: Change the settings of a plugin
put.description: Replaces the settings. Every value is checked against what the plugin declares, a field it does not declare is refused, and a secret field must name an existing vault secret of the right kind. Which fields changed is recorded, never the values.

get.summary: The compose fragment that runs the container of a plugin
get.description: For a plugin whose code runs as a sidecar container: a Docker Compose file that adds the container to the stack on an internal network with no way out, read-only, without privileges, with the memory and cpu the manifest names and the image pinned by digest. It holds the token with which the sidecar proves itself to the core, derived from the plugin and its digest: keep it like a secret. Swellwright never starts a container itself.

post.summary: What a sidecar asks of the core
post.description: Called by a plugin's container, not by people: it proves itself with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, the token of the compose fragment. The core does what the plugin was approved for and nothing else: requests to the approved hosts, the secret bound to a setting, the plugin's own storage. The answer is always 200 with `ok`; a refusal says why. A wrong token, a plugin that is not enabled or whose files changed answer 401.

get.description: The inventory, ordered by name, each server with how many host keys are pinned, how many access entries it has and a summary of its facts. The filters combine.

schema.description: Only servers that carry this tag.
Servers whose name or address contains this text, ignoring case.

post.summary: Add a server
post.description: A taken name answers 409. The server starts as a draft unless a state is given.

get.description: With its pinned host keys, its access entries (the names of the secrets, never their values) and its facts.

patch.description: Any field, including the state: the five states may follow one another freely, and the audit record keeps the old and the new one. A taken name answers 409.

delete.description: Only a draft or a retired server; any other state answers 409. Its host keys, access entries and facts go with it; the vault secrets stay.

post.summary: Pin a host key by hand
post.description: Pins a fingerprint the person checked (for example from the provider console). Idempotent: pinning the same fingerprint again changes nothing and answers 200 with the key that is there; a new key answers 201.

delete.description: For a server that was reinstalled: the old key must stop being trusted. Nothing connects to a server whose keys are all revoked until a new one is pinned.

post.summary: Add a way to log in
post.description: The entry names vault secrets and holds no value. A password entry needs a secret of kind `ssh_password`, a key entry one of kind `ssh_key`, and the sudo secret one of kind `ssh_password`; anything else answers 400, as does a secret that does not exist. A server has at most five entries (409 beyond that). A secret in use cannot be deleted from the vault.

patch.summary: Change a way to log in
patch.description: The same rules as when adding: the result must be consistent.

delete.summary: Remove a way to log in
delete.description: The secrets it named stay in the vault.

post.summary: Read the host key the server shows
post.description: Connects to the server and reads its SSH host key without sending any credential, then compares it with the pinned ones. Nothing is stored (only an audit note): the person checks the fingerprint against another source and then calls `accept`. `differs` means keys are pinned and this one is not among them: expected after the operating system was reinstalled, a sign of somebody in the middle otherwise. It sends no credential, but it makes the API open a connection to the server, so it needs the same role (`servers:write`) as the other SSH operations; a role that may only read never causes a connection. Errors: 404, 409 `address_not_allowed`, 429 `rate_limited`, 502 `ssh_connect_failed`, 504 `ssh_timeout`.

post.summary: Pin the host key the person confirmed
post.description: Reads the key again and pins it only when it is exactly the fingerprint the person confirmed (otherwise 409 `host_key_mismatch`, nothing stored), with the source `scan`. Pinning a key that is pinned already changes nothing and answers 200. When other keys are pinned, a different key needs `replace: true`, which revokes them in the same step (the operating system was reinstalled); without it: 409 `host_key_replace_required`. Both the pin and the revocations are audit records. Other errors: 404, 409 `address_not_allowed`, 429, 502 `ssh_connect_failed`, 504 `ssh_timeout`.

post.summary: Try an access entry
post.description: Logs in with that entry (the host key must be pinned and is checked before any credential is sent) and runs read-only probes: `id -un`, `id -u` and a sudo check (with the stored sudo secret on standard input when there is one, otherwise `sudo -n`). A login that does not work is a result: 200 with `ok: false` and the code and message. The time and the outcome are kept on the entry. Errors: 404 (no such server or entry), 409 `host_key_not_pinned` (nothing is pinned yet), `host_key_mismatch` (the server shows another key than the pinned one: `details` has `expected` and `actual`), `address_not_allowed` (the outbound policy refuses the address), 423 `vault_sealed`, 429 `rate_limited`.

post.summary: Collect the facts of a server
post.description: Runs a fixed, read-only script over SSH (as root, or through sudo when the login is not root and sudo works, or as the login), parses its output strictly and stores the result; a malformed part becomes a warning and the rest is kept. Access entries are tried by priority until one logs in. One refresh per server runs at a time: a second request joins it. Errors: 404 (no such server or entry), 409 `host_key_not_pinned` (nothing is pinned yet), `host_key_mismatch` (the server shows another key than the pinned one: `details` has `expected` and `actual`), `address_not_allowed` (the outbound policy refuses the address), 423 `vault_sealed`, 429 `rate_limited`. Also 409 `no_access_entry`, 502 `ssh_connect_failed`, `ssh_auth_failed`, `ssh_key_invalid`, `ssh_failed`, `facts_unreadable`, 504 `ssh_timeout`.

get.description: What the last refresh found, with when, what collected it and the hash of the script. 404 until facts were collected. Reading never connects to the server.

message.description: Human-readable text for logs and developers, not for branching.

requestId.description: Also sent in the x-request-id response header.

details.description: Optional structured details, for example validation issues.

latencyMs.description: How long the check took, in milliseconds.

error.description: Short reason when the check is down; never contains secrets.

version.description: Semantic version of the running build.

commit.description: Source revision, when the build embeds it.

time.description: When the image was built, as the build recorded it (usually ISO 8601).

number.description: The number of the build in the CI that made it.

build.description: What the build recorded about itself. A field is null when the build did not say.

branch.description: The branch the build was made from.

commit.description: The source revision (the full or abbreviated hash).

commitUrl.description: The page of that revision on GitHub; null unless the revision is a hash.

git.description: The source of the build. A field is null when the build did not say.

enabled.description: False when the administrator switched the check off (`SW_UPDATE_CHECK=off`).

latestVersion.description: The newest published release, without a leading "v". Null while it is not known yet, when the repository has no release, or when the check is off.

stars.description: How many people starred the repository; null while not known.

repositoryUrl.description: The page of the repository (taken from the settings, no request needed).

checkedAt.description: When the server last learned something from GitHub; null while it has not.

UpdatesResponse.description: What the server knows about newer releases and the project page.

language.description: The language the person chose; null until they do (the console follows the browser).

initialized.description: True once the instance owner exists.

setupToken.description: The one-time token the server printed to its log at start.

next.description: `totp`: enter a code from the authenticator or a recovery code. `totp_enrollment`: set up the authenticator first.

PendingSession.description: The password was accepted; a second step is needed to finish signing in.

code.description: A 6-digit authenticator code, or one recovery code (only on sign-in).

otpauthUri.description: An otpauth:// URI for QR codes.

permissions.description: What the user's role allows. The console uses it to show or hide pages; every route checks again.

expiresAt.description: When the session ends if it stays idle.

language.description: The language to use after signing in; null: follow the browser again.

permissions.description: What the user's role allows. The console uses it to show or hide pages; every route checks again.

recoveryCodes.description: Single-use codes for a lost authenticator. Shown once, never again.

RoleCatalog.description: The built-in roles with their permission sets, and the permission catalogue.

AuditOutcome.description: `success`: it happened. `failure`: it was tried and did not work (a wrong password). `denied`: the caller may not do it.

seq.description: Position in the chain, from 1, without gaps.

name.description: The login name at the time of the event.

actor.description: Null when nobody was identified (an unknown account, a refused setup).

action.description: One of the known actions; later versions add more.

prevHash.description: The hash of the previous event; zeros for the first one.

total.description: How many events match the filters (and the cursor), whatever `limit` and `offset` say: the page count of a table.

seq.description: The first sequence number that does not check out.

reason.description: `missing`: a number is absent or repeated. `link`: the previous hash does not match. `content`: the stored hash does not match the stored fields.

checked.description: How many events were checked and found intact, up to the first problem.

head.description: The last event when the check started. Note it somewhere outside the database.

events.description: Oldest first, with every field a hash covers.

nextFrom.description: The `from` of the next page; null when this page reaches the end of the log.

head.description: The last event of the whole log when the page was read.

AuditExport.description: A page of the log in the form that can be checked offline: the events with their hashes, in order. A file is the lines `{"format":"swellwright-audit-export","version":1}` followed by one event per line.

checkpoint.description: Opaque text that names the last event and carries a signature only this instance can make. Store it somewhere outside the database.

result.description: `ok`: the chain up to the checkpoint is intact and the event is what it was. `malformed`: not a checkpoint. `not_ours`: the signature is wrong (another instance, or made up). `event_missing`: the log is shorter than the checkpoint says (a tail was cut off). `hash_differs`: the event at that number is not the one the checkpoint saw (history was rewritten). `chain_broken`: the chain up to that event does not check out.

eventsSince.description: How many events were added after the checkpoint; null when it could not be checked.

token.description: The invitation token the owner handed over.

elevatedUntil.description: Until when this session counts as freshly verified (step-up authentication).

invitationExpiresAt.description: When the open invitation of this user stops working; null when there is none.

token.description: Shown once, never again; only its hash is kept. The console opens `#invite=<token>`.

Invitation.description: A one-time token that lets its holder choose a password for the account.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Fields that are absent stay as they are; `null` clears the display name or the e-mail address.

state.description: `uninitialized`: no vault yet. `sealed`: it exists and the key is not in memory. `unsealed`: it can be used.

passphraseChangedAt.description: Null: never changed since the vault was set up.

recoveryKey.description: Shown once, never stored. With it the vault can be opened when the passphrase is lost: keep it away from this server.

version.description: Moves forward every time the value is replaced.

SecretView.description: A secret without its value. Values are write-only.

expiresAt.description: When the session ends if it stays idle.

absoluteExpiresAt.description: When the session ends whatever its activity.

current.description: True for the session that made this request.

elevated.description: Whether it is freshly verified with the second factor right now (step-up).

prefix.description: The first characters of the token, to recognise it in a list.

ipAllowlist.description: Addresses or ranges it may be used from; empty: anywhere.

token.description: The token. Shown once, never again; only its hash is kept. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

network.description: Hosts it may call, as host:port, only through the core.

secrets.description: Kinds of secret it may be handed, for one call.

panel.description: Scopes of the panel API it may use.

ssh.description: Whether it may run commands on servers.

widens.description: It may do more than what was approved.

mode.description: Runs its own code, or is described in data.

calls.description: Calls made since the process started.

lastError.description: Why it failed; null while it has not.

modules.description: What the process loaded: each extension kind and the methods it offers.

approvedBy.description: The user name at the time.

PluginApproval.description: What an administrator approved, and when.

id.description: The plugin id; for a directory that is not a plugin, its name.

folder.description: The directory name; null when it is gone.

discovery.description: Null when the plugin is gone.

problems.description: Why it is invalid or incompatible.

permissions.description: What its files ask for now.

digest.description: SHA-256 over every file of the plugin; approval is tied to it.

signed.description: The manifest carries a signature. It is not verified yet, so it proves nothing.

hasSettings.description: It brings a settings page of its own.

hasConfig.description: It has settings of its own to fill in (a `config.schema`).

sidecar.description: How its container is run, when its code runs as a sidecar (ADR 0031).

change.description: For a changed plugin: what its permissions differ by from the approved ones.

digest.description: The digest of the plugin as shown; the plugin is enabled only if it is still this.

choices.description: A closed list of values, if there is one.

secretKind.description: Set: the field holds the id of a vault secret of this kind (for example `dns-oauth`).

values.description: What is set now, defaults applied. A secret field holds the id of a secret, or null.

problems.description: What is wrong with the stored settings for the plugin as it is now (a field it added).

service.description: The name of the compose service of the sidecar.

compose.description: The compose file to add to the stack. It holds the plugin's token: keep it like a secret.

coreUrl.description: Where the sidecar reaches Swellwright from its network.

message.description: Why the core refused, when `ok` is false.

value.description: A new value. Needs the vault open; the version moves forward.

UpdateSecretRequest.description: Fields that are absent stay as they are; `null` clears the description or the expiry.

value.description: The secret. Not kept anywhere by the console after it is hidden.

os.description: For example "Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS"; null when the facts do not say.

collectedAs.description: With which rights the script ran: as root, as the login through sudo, or as the plain login. Some facts (listening processes, `sshd` settings, the firewall, containers) need root.

bootedAt.description: The server clock minus the uptime.

disks.description: `/` and the mounts of real block devices; not tmpfs, snaps or overlays.

utc.description: The server clock when it was read.

skewSeconds.description: Server clock minus this server, in seconds (positive: the server is ahead).

listeningPorts.description: TCP sockets in the LISTEN state.

state.description: The state systemd reports; `not_installed` when there is no such unit.

versions.description: Null for a program that is not installed.

imageTag.description: The tag of the image, which names the version of a node.

containers.description: Docker containers, running or not; null without docker or without the right to ask it.

upgradable.description: Packages an upgrade would change, by the package lists the server already has: nothing is fetched.

warnings.description: What was malformed or cut off; the rest is intact.

scriptSha256.description: The SHA-256 of the script that ran on the server; null for facts of an earlier version.

pinned.description: At least one host key is pinned: a connection can be trusted.

source.description: `manual` (typed in) or `scan` (read from the server and confirmed).

acceptedBy.description: The login name of the user who pinned it; null when that user no longer exists.

SecretRef.description: A vault secret by name. The value is never part of a server.

secret.description: The password or the private key.

sudoSecret.description: The password used for `sudo`, when there is one.

priority.description: Lower first: the order in which the entries are tried.

lastVerifiedAt.description: When the entry was last tried; null if never.

lastVerifyOk.description: Whether that try logged in and ran its checks; null if never tried.

UpdateServerRequest.description: Fields that are absent stay as they are; `null` clears the country, the provider or the notes; `tags` replaces the list.

secretId.description: A vault secret of the kind the method needs.

sudoSecretId.description: A vault secret of kind `ssh_password`, used for `sudo`.

priority.description: Lower first; after the last entry by default.

UpdateAccessRequest.description: Fields that are absent stay as they are; `null` removes the sudo secret. The result must still be consistent: the secret kind has to fit the method.

address.description: The address that was asked, as the inventory has it.

status.description: `new`: nothing is pinned yet. `pinned`: this key is one of the pinned ones. `differs`: keys are pinned and this is none of them, which after a reinstall of the operating system is expected, and otherwise may be somebody in the middle.

pinned.description: The keys that are pinned now.

fingerprintSha256.description: The fingerprint the person was shown and confirmed. The server is asked again and must show exactly this key.

replace.description: Required when other keys are pinned: they are revoked in the same step (the operating system was reinstalled).

replaced.description: How many pinned keys were revoked.

ok.description: The login worked and the check commands ran.

latencyMs.description: How long the whole check took.

sudo.description: `not_needed`: the login is root. `ok`: sudo works (without a password, or with the stored one). `password_required`: sudo asks for a password and none is stored. `failed`: sudo refused. `unavailable`: sudo is not installed, or the check did not get that far.

error.description: Why the check failed, when it did.

session.name: sw_session
session.description: Set by the sign-in routes. Routes marked as needing a session accept a signed-in one; the second sign-in step accepts one whose password was accepted.

bearer.description: An API token (`swt_...`) created in the console. It carries a subset of the permissions of its owner, expires, and is refused on every route that needs a fresh second factor.
